description: Issue #20 — User Registration, Login, and Profile Management. Fixes the role escalation vulnerability in RegisterRequest and AuthService, adds transactional and concurrent-duplicate-email safety to AuthService, enforces inactive-account rejection in login, creates UserProfileRequest and UserProfileResponse DTOs, creates UserController with GET/PUT /api/v1/users/me, and adds the full test suite for auth and profile. Depends on FEAT-001 (H2 and exception handler fixes must be in place before tests run).
steps: Modify RegisterRequest.java: REMOVE the 'role' field (and its default value 'Role.CUSTOMER') entirely. The field must not appear in the class — callers cannot supply a role at all. Remove the 'import com.vps.entity.User.Role' import if it becomes unused. File: c:\Users\thrup\OneDrive\Desktop\SE\Project-Team-10\src\backend\src\main\java\com\vps\dto\RegisterRequest.java.

Modify AuthService.java: (a) Remove the conditional role assignment 'request.getRole() != null ? request.getRole() : User.Role.CUSTOMER' and replace with the hardcoded 'user.setRole(User.Role.CUSTOMER)'. (b) Add @Transactional to the register() method (import org.springframework.transaction.annotation.Transactional). (c) Wrap the existsByEmail check + save in a try/catch for DataIntegrityViolationException (import org.springframework.dao.DataIntegrityViolationException): catch it and throw new IllegalArgumentException("Email already registered") so the GlobalExceptionHandler returns 400 — this handles the race condition where two concurrent requests both pass the existsByEmail check before either commits. (d) In login(), after the isLocked check, add an isActive check: if (!user.isActive()) throw new IllegalStateException("Account is inactive. Please contact administrator.") — this returns 403 via GlobalExceptionHandler. (e) Add @Transactional to the login() method. File: c:\Users\thrup\OneDrive\Desktop\SE\Project-Team-10\src\backend\src\main\java\com\vps\service\AuthService.java.

Use @Data and @NoArgsConstructor (Lombok). Import com.vps.entity.User.Role. No passwordHash field. Add @Transactional to updateUserProfile. File: c:\Users\thrup\OneDrive\Desktop\SE\Project-Team-10\src\backend\src\main\java\com\vps\service\AuthService.java.

Create UserController.java. Annotate with @RestController, @RequestMapping("/api/v1/users"), @RequiredArgsConstructor. Inject AuthService. Implement: GET /me — extract email from @AuthenticationPrincipal UserDetails, call authService.getUserProfile(email), return ResponseEntity.ok(ApiResponse.success("Profile retrieved", response)). PUT /me — extract email, @Valid @RequestBody UserProfileRequest, call authService.updateUserProfile(email, request), return ResponseEntity.ok(ApiResponse.success("Profile updated", response)). Both endpoints derive identity from the JWT principal — no client-supplied user ID is accepted. Create AuthServiceTest.java. Use @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class). Mock UserRepository, PasswordEncoder, JwtUtil, AuditLogService. Test cases: (1) register_success — mock existsByEmail=false, passwordEncoder.encode returns hash, userRepo.save returns user, jwtUtil.generateToken returns token — assert token, role=CUSTOMER, no passwordHash in response. (2) register_duplicateEmail — mock existsByEmail=true — assert throws IllegalArgumentException. (3) register_roleCannotBeElevated — call register with a RegisterRequest that has no role field (role field removed) — verify saved user has role=CUSTOMER. (4) register_concurrentDuplicate — mock existsByEmail=false but userRepo.save throws DataIntegrityViolationException — assert throws IllegalArgumentException. (5) login_success — mock findByEmail, passwordEncoder.matches=true — assert token returned and failedAttempts reset to 0. (6) login_invalidPassword — mock matches=false — assert throws IllegalArgumentException and failedAttempts incremented. (7) login_accountLocked — set user.isLocked=true — assert throws IllegalStateException. (8) login_inactiveAccount — set user.isActive=false — assert throws IllegalStateException. (9) login_lockAfterFiveFailures — simulate 4 prior failed attempts, password wrong again — assert user.isLocked=true. Create AuthControllerTest.java. Use @SpringBootTest(webEnvironment=RANDOM_PORT) + @AutoConfigureMockMvc + @ActiveProfiles("test"). Test cases via MockMvc: (1) POST /api/v1/auth/register with valid body — assert HTTP 201, response has token, role=CUSTOMER. (2) POST /api/v1/auth/register with duplicate email — assert HTTP 400. (3) POST /api/v1/auth/register with role field present in JSON (e.g. 'role':'ADMINISTRATOR') — assert HTTP 201 AND response body role=CUSTOMER (role field on RegisterRequest is gone so it is ignored). (4) POST /api/v1/auth/register with weak password (no special char) — assert HTTP 400. (5) POST /api/v1/auth/login with valid credentials — assert HTTP 200, token present. (6) POST /api/v1/auth/login with wrong password — assert HTTP 400. (7) POST /api/v1/auth/login on locked account — assert HTTP 403. File: c:\Users\thrup\OneDrive\Desktop\SE\Project-Team-10\src\backend\src\test\java\com\vps\controller\AuthControllerTest.java.

acceptance_criteria: AuthService.register() always sets role=CUSTOMER regardless of request body.
AuthService.register() is annotated @Transactional and catches DataIntegrityViolationException.
AuthService.login() rejects inactive accounts with IllegalStateException (→ HTTP 403 via GlobalExceptionHandler).
GET /api/v1/users/me returns 200 with UserProfileResponse for authenticated user.
PUT /api/v1/users/me updates fullName and phone only; role, id, email, isActive, passwordHash cannot be changed via this endpoint.
No response from /api/v1/users/me contains a passwordHash field.
mvn test passes all AuthServiceTest, AuthControllerTest, and UserControllerTest cases.
verification: cd c:\Users\thrup\OneDrive\Desktop\SE\Project-Team-10\src\backend && mvn test -pl . -Dtest=AuthServiceTest,AuthControllerTest,UserControllerTest — all tests must pass.
findings: Two additional fixes were required beyond the stated steps: (1) application-test.properties needed an explicit 'spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.dialect=org.hibernate.dialect.H2Dialect' property to override the MySQLDialect set in application.properties — without this override, Hibernate generated MySQL-specific DDL (engine=InnoDB) that H2 cannot parse, causing all Spring Boot integration tests to fail during application context startup. (2) Byte Buddy (used by Mockito for mocking) does not officially support Java 25 (only up to Java 23). This caused all @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) unit tests to fail with 'Java 25 (69) is not supported'. The fix was to add a maven-surefire-plugin configuration block in pom.xml with argLine '-Dnet.bytebuddy.experimental=true', which enables Byte Buddy's experimental Java 25 support. These are infrastructure changes that do not affect runtime behavior. Final test results: AuthServiceTest 9/9, AuthControllerTest 7/7, UserControllerTest 5/5 — all 21 tests passed.
